capabilities: Start a local Node.js server that serves the vault in a browser
Browse, search, and edit Markdown notes with autosave
Render Markdown tables and Mermaid diagrams in browser preview
Follow wiki links and inspect outgoing links and backlinks
Import desktop theme colors and fonts into the browser interface
disambiguation: Despite the name, it is not a web publishing or hosting tool; the server runs only on your machine and serves the vault to your own browser.
extras: Desktop-only. README warns that the plugin starts a local Node.js process that can read and write vault files, so it should only be used on trusted computers and vaults; the manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian is a desktop app, so there is no built-in way to read and write vault notes in a regular browser tab alongside web pages or on a split screen.
summary: Local-server plugin that opens and edits the current vault in a desktop browser tab via a Node.js server on 127.0.0.1.
